x: The Moon's mean distance is 384,400 km; it varies from about 363,300 km (perigee) to 405,500 km (apogee). None of the options is exact, and 364 thousand km (about the perigee distance) is the only one inside the Moon's real range, so it is the key.
source: NASA NSSDC Moon Fact Sheet (nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/moonfact.html: semimajor axis 0.3844, perigee 0.3633, apogee 0.4055 × 10^6 km); Rocket General Geography p.8 (average distance 384,400 km)
evidence: NASA NSSDC Moon Fact Sheet: mean 384,400 km, perigee 363,300 km, apogee 405,500 km
Rocket General Geography p.8: average distance 384,400 km
PMF Physical Geography 01 p.50: about 3,84,400 km
NextGen Indian Geography APPSC 01 p.3: perigee ~360,000 km, apogee ~405,000 km
dispute: Key: 364 thousand km. Strictly the mean distance is 384,400 km (NASA); 364,000 km is roughly the perigee (closest) distance.

x: Of the options the USA is largest by total area (about 98 lakh sq km incl. coastal/territorial waters, CIA) – usual book order Russia, Canada, USA, China, Brazil, Australia. The printed key (c) China contradicts the book's own explanation (Canada, USA, China, Brazil), so it is a misprint.
source: Wikipedia 'List of countries and dependencies by area' (UN Statistics Division / CIA figures and footnotes on US vs China); NextGen Rocket World Geography p.2; PMF World Geography 04 p.25 (Brazil 5th), 05 p.29 (Australia 6th)
dispute: Most books: USA is 3rd and China 4th by total area (CIA figure 9.83 million sq km incl. coastal and territorial waters). Strictly, excluding those waters (UN) and by land area, China (9.60 / 9.33 million sq km) is larger than the USA (9.53 / 9.15), and some keys give China.
evidence: Wikipedia list by area: US 9,525,067 sq km excl. coastal/territorial waters (UN) vs China 9,596,960; land: China 9,326,410 vs US 9,147,593; footnote: US ranks ahead only when its coastal and territorial waters are included
printed explanation in the source book: order Canada, U.S.A., China, Brazil
